objective: Add a Sobol sensitivity mission type that apportions output variance across the input spreads before any uncertainty reduction campaign is priced
rationale: The lab propagates input spreads through Monte Carlo but never says which input owns the variance, so reduction work is untargeted. Variance-based decomposition gives main and total effect indices per input; on the reduced-order paths an evaluation costs about a millisecond, so a pick-and-freeze design of N times (M plus 2) evaluations at N of 200 is seconds of compute for the valve and comparable for the airliner surrogate. The mission ends with a ranking of inputs by variance share and a recommendation of where the next samples or the next measurement effort should go. Offline evidence measured 2026-07-25: on the valve screen discharge coefficient owns the variance (main 0.61, total 0.60) over flow amplitude (main 0.39); on the airliner sizing chain non-wing drag owns it (main 0.64) over payload mass (main 0.35); the estimator recovers the Ishigami closed-form indices to 0.022 absolute and every Sobol identity holds within bootstrap CI.
citations: Dakota Theory Manual, Stochastic Expansion Methods, Sandia National Laboratories
Dakota Reference Manual, Sampling With Variance Based Decomposition, Sandia National Laboratories
expected_knowledge_gain: Main and total effect Sobol indices for the valve inputs (flow amplitude 5 percent, discharge coefficient 6 percent) and the airliner inputs (span, area, sweep, taper), plus a standing answer to which spread is worth buying down first
launch_prompt: Run a Sobol sensitivity mission on the valve screen: inputs are flow amplitude (sigma 5 percent) and discharge coefficient (sigma 6 percent); evaluate the cycle-weighted loss through the reduced-order orifice path with a pick-and-freeze design, N 200, cost N times (M plus 2) equals 800 evaluations; report main and total effect indices with bootstrap confidence intervals, then repeat on the airliner input spreads through the fitted surrogate with one confirming solver run at the highest-index corner. Present the result as a variance-share bar per input with the earned-badge convention.

evidence.standard_stage: Stage 2 - offline evidence on a benchmark

outcome: The mission ships as a routed act and apportions the variance of two screens over their own published spreads. Discharge coefficient owns 0.584 [0.527, 0.648] of the valve loss variance against 0.430 [0.370, 0.488] for flow amplitude; non-wing drag owns 0.664 [0.587, 0.741] of the airliner lift-to-drag variance against 0.314 [0.258, 0.376] for payload mass. The approved design of 200 base samples settled neither case, so the act doubles to 800 and reports the budget the ranking rests on. 11200 evaluations, 0.44 s measured against a 6 core-minute estimate. Gate criteria now sit in docs/physics_rules.yaml.
